'''Prospect Lefferts Gardens''' is a residential neighborhood in [[Flatbush]] of the [[New York City]] [[Boroughs of New York City|borough]] of [[Brooklyn]]. The community is bounded by Empire Boulevard (formerly Malbone Street) to the north, Clarkson Avenue to the south, New York Avenue to the east, and [[Ocean Avenue (Brooklyn)|Ocean Avenue]]/[[Prospect Park (Brooklyn)|Prospect Park]] to the west.<ref>{{cite news |title=Prospect-Lefferts Gardens; Convenient and Close-Knit Yet Diverse |first=Dulcie |last=Leimbach |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/04/04/realestate/if-you-re-thinking-living-prospect-lefferts-gardens-convenient-close-knit-yet.html |newspaper=The New York Times |date=April 4, 2004 |access-date=January 22, 2010}}</ref> Prospect Lefferts Gardens was designated a New York City Landmark area in 1979 and called the Prospect Lefferts Gardens Historic District.<ref name="ldmrk_nyc"/>

The neighborhood contains an ethnically diverse community with a largely [[West Indian Americans|Caribbean-American]] and [[African-American]] population.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.point2homes.com/US/Neighborhood/NY/Brooklyn/Prospect-Lefferts-Garden-Demographics.html |title=Prospect – Lefferts Gardens |publisher=point2homes.com |access-date=November 21, 2015}}</ref> Since the 2000s, Prospect Lefferts Gardens has been [[gentrification|gentrifying]] quickly. Real estate development has increased and new residents from other groups have increased.<ref name="nytimes :0">{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/03/16/realestate/prospect-lefferts-gardens-is-on-the-map.html|title=Prospect-Lefferts Gardens Is 'On the Map' |newspaper=The New York Times |date=March 13, 2014 |access-date=January 13, 2015 |author=Alison Gregor}}</ref>

Prospect Lefferts Gardens is part of [[Brooklyn Community Board 9|Brooklyn Community District 9]], and its primary [[ZIP Code]] is 11225.<ref name="NYCPlanning"/> It is patrolled by the 71st Precinct of the [[New York City Police Department]].<ref name="NYPD 71st Precinct"/> Politically it is represented by the [[New York City Council]]'s 40th District.<ref>[http://www.nyc.gov/html/dc/downloads/pdf/brooklyn.pdf Current City Council Districts for Kings County], [[New York City]]. Accessed May 5, 2017.</ref>

==Name==

The name Prospect Lefferts Gardens was created in 1968 by the Prospect Lefferts Gardens Neighborhood Association (PLGNA). Prospect Lefferts Gardens is a combination of the names of three nearby locations: [[Prospect Park (Brooklyn)|Prospect Park]], [[Lefferts Manor Historic District|Lefferts Manor]], and the [[Brooklyn Botanic Garden]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://explorebk.com/2015/02/04/brooklyn-neighborhoods-got-names-part-5-boerum-hill-crown-heights-lefferts-gardens-sunset-park/ |title=How Brooklyn neighborhoods got their names part 5: Boerum Hill, Crown Heights, Prospect Lefferts Gardens, and Sunset Park |author=Emily Nonko |work=Explore Brooklyn |access-date=November 21, 2015 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20151122072243/http://explorebk.com/2015/02/04/brooklyn-neighborhoods-got-names-part-5-boerum-hill-crown-heights-lefferts-gardens-sunset-park/ |archive-date=November 22, 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://ny.curbed.com/archives/2014/06/13/why_prospect_lefferts_gardens_will_never_be_heights_park.php |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150210042829/http://ny.curbed.com/archives/2014/06/13/why_prospect_lefferts_gardens_will_never_be_heights_park.php |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 10, 2015 |title=Why Prospect Lefferts Gardens Will Never Be 'Heights Park' |work=Curbed NY |date=June 13, 2014 |access-date=November 21, 2015}}</ref> Lefferts Manor is named for the Dutch colonial family who built it; they were also one of the largest owners of slaves in Brooklyn.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Morris)|first=Suzanne Spellen (aka Montrose|date=2010-12-02|title=Lefferts Family {{!}} Brooklyn History|url=https://www.brownstoner.com/brooklyn-life/walkabout-the-l-2/|access-date=2021-04-16|website=Brownstoner|language=en-US}}</ref>

==History==

The area was originally settled by a [[Dutch colonization of the Americas|Dutch]] family in 1665, at which time it was within the [[Flatbush, Brooklyn|Town of Flatbush]]. In 1893 the Lefferts estate was divided by James Lefferts into 600 building lots, now known as Lefferts Manor, and sold to developers. Lefferts observed construction from the [[Lefferts Historic House|Lefferts homestead]], then located on Flatbush Avenue between Maple and Midwood Streets (now a historic museum located in Prospect Park).<ref name="Brooklyn Daily Eagle">{{cite news |title=On This Day in History: Prospect-Lefferts Gardens Become Historic District |url=http://www.brooklyneagle.com/categories/category.php?category_id=23&id=23675 |newspaper=Brooklyn Daily Eagle |date=October 9, 2008 |access-date=January 22, 2010}}</ref> In order to ensure that the neighborhood would contain homes of a substantial nature, Lefferts attached land-use deed restrictions, dictating that each lot contain a single family residence built of brick or stone at least two stories in height, among other restrictions. The [[Restrictive covenant|land-use covenant]] still exists in Lefferts Manor.<ref>[http://leffertsmanor.org/history.shtml The Origins of Lefferts Manor]. Retrieved November 13, 2006 {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061110014427/http://www.leffertsmanor.org/history.shtml |date=November 10, 2006 }}</ref> Houses in Lefferts Manor were mostly constructed during the late 19th century and early 20th century, the last of which were constructed in the early 1950s. Patio Gardens, the last large development built before the wave of gentrification in the mid-2000s, was constructed in the early 1960s.<ref name="nytimes :0"/>

Lefferts Manor and parts of Lefferts Avenue and Sterling Street, not in the single-family covenant, were granted landmark status by the [[New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission]] on October 9, 1979.<ref name="ldmrk_nyc">{{cite web |url=http://www.nyc.gov/html/lpc/downloads/pdf/reports/PROSPECT_LEFFERTS_GARDENS_HISTORIC_DISTRICT.pdf |title=PROSPECT LEFFERTS GARDENS HISTORIC DISTRICT DESIGNATION REPORT |date=October 9, 1979 |access-date=March 16, 2018 |last1=Dolkart |first1=Andrew S. |first2=Luella |last2=Boddewyn |first3=Douglas |last3=Brenner |first4=Rachel |last4=Carley |first5=Anthony |last5=Robins |publisher=City of New York |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170218051249/https://www1.nyc.gov/html/lpc/downloads/pdf/reports/PROSPECT_LEFFERTS_GARDENS_HISTORIC_DISTRICT.pdf |archive-date=February 18, 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The [[Lefferts Manor Historic District]] was listed on the [[National Register of Historic Places]] in 1992.<ref name="nris"/>  In 2009 the neighborhood gained a second landmark district when the New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission designated the Ocean on the Park Historic District. As a small, early 20th century enclave that is set-back from the street, this historic district consists of only 2 brick and 10 limestone townhouses. Yet it stands in striking architectural contrast to the long line of large and stately apartment buildings which otherwise dominate Ocean Avenue at the southeastern border of Prospect Park.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nyc.gov/html/lpc/downloads/pdf/reports/Ocean_ParkHD_desigrep.pdf |title=Ocean On The Park Historic District |access-date=January 23, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100607231719/http://www.nyc.gov/html/lpc/downloads/pdf/reports/Ocean_ParkHD_desigrep.pdf |archive-date=June 7, 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2014 a third small historic district–Chester Court, a cull-de-sac off the west side of Flatbush Avenue, near Rutland Road, was designated. The Chester Court Historic District has 18 Tudor-revival townhouses, similar to those on Rutland Road in the main Historic District.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 16, 2018 |title=Chester Court Historic District {{!}} HDC |url=https://hdc.org/buildings/chester-court-historic-district/ |access-date=2026-06-14 |language=en-US}}</ref> The Prospect Lefferts Gardens Historic District was nominated<ref>{{Cite web |title=New York Nominations to the National Register |url=https://www.brownstoner.com/architecture/national-register-nominations-new-york-state-2023-cypress-hills/ |access-date=2026-06-14 |website=www.brownstoner.com |language=en-US}}</ref> and later added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2023.<ref name="weeklylist 2023">{{cite web |title=National Register of Historic Places Weekly Lists 2023 |url=https://www.nps.gov/subjects/nationalregister/upload/Weekly-List-2023-508.pdf |publisher=National Park Service |access-date=2026-06-14}}</ref>

[[File:Marvinplgarts2.jpg|thumb|275px|left|Artists paint murals along Lincoln Road]]

Concurrent with the development of Lefferts Manor was the growth of the surrounding area, now known collectively as Prospect Lefferts Gardens. Many one and two family homes were constructed in the early 20th century.<ref name="Brooklyn Daily Eagle"/> Presently, other areas of Prospect Lefferts Gardens contain a mixture of single-family and multi-family homes as well as larger apartment houses.<ref name="nytimes :0"/>

Since the 1960s, Caribbean immigrants have settled in Prospect Lefferts Gardens as well as in surrounding areas such as [[East Flatbush, Brooklyn|East Flatbush]], [[Flatbush, Brooklyn|Flatbush]], and [[Crown Heights, Brooklyn|Crown Heights]]. The overlapping sections of these neighborhoods were nicknamed ''[[Little Caribbean, Brooklyn|Little Caribbean]]'' on [[Google Maps]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.littlecaribbean.nyc/ |title=Little Caribbean NYC}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dnainfo.com/new-york/20170926/flatbush/flatbush-little-caribbean-neighborhood-designation/|title=Flatbush to Become City's First 'Little Caribbean' Neighborhood This Week}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.garrettleight.com/blogs/stories/neighborhood-guide-brooklyn-s-little-caribbean|title=Neighborhood Guide: Brooklyn's Little Caribbean|date=April 29, 2021 }}</ref>

==Community organizations==
Prospect Lefferts Gardens has a long tradition of community participation and involvement. In 2009,  PLG Arts transformed multiple drab-looking construction facades into murals that reflected the area and its artists. LinRoFORMA, founded 2010, organizes Lincoln Road residents and businesses to revitalize the street and neighborhood. PLG Community Supported Agriculture links the community and a [[Connecticut]] farm, bringing organic produce and vegetables to residents and providing sustainability for future growth. Strong interest in improved food options led to the formation of the Lefferts Community Food Cooperative in 2009, a  market that uses cooperative principles to sell socially responsible and healthy food products. The Maple Street Community Garden, founded in 2012 at 237 Maple St., is a communally managed organic vegetable garden open to the public, and runs an active composting program. Other organizations include the Lefferts Manor Association, which was founded in 1919 to enforce the single family covenant; and PLGNA, the Prospect Lefferts Gardens Neighborhood Association, founded 1968.

==Demographics==
Based on data from the [[2010 United States census]], the population of Prospect Lefferts Gardens was 67,459, a change of −2,841 (−4.2%) from the 70,300 counted in [[2000 United States census|2000]]. Covering an area of {{convert|726.33|acres}}, the neighborhood had a population density of {{convert|92.9|PD/acre|PD/sqmi PD/sqkm}}.<ref name=PLP5>[http://www1.nyc.gov/assets/planning/download/pdf/data-maps/nyc-population/census2010/t_pl_p5_nta.pdf Table PL-P5 NTA: Total Population and Persons Per Acre – New York City Neighborhood Tabulation Areas*, 2010], Population Division – [[New York City]] Department of City Planning, February 2012. Accessed June 16, 2016.</ref> The racial makeup of the neighborhood was 9.6% (6,495) [[White (U.S. census)|White]], 76.5% (51,578) [[African American (U.S. census)|African American]], 0.2% (155) [[Native American (U.S. census)|Native American]], 1.6% (1,063) [[Asian (U.S. census)|Asian]], 0% (17) [[Pacific Islander (U.S. census)|Pacific Islander]], 0.4% (292) from [[Race (United States census)|other races]], and 1.8% (1,231) from two or more races. [[Hispanic (U.S. census)|Hispanic]] or [[Latino (U.S. census)|Latino]] of any race were 9.8% (6,628) of the population.<ref name=PLP3A>[http://www1.nyc.gov/assets/planning/download/pdf/data-maps/nyc-population/census2010/t_pl_p3a_nta.pdf Table PL-P3A NTA: Total Population by Mutually Exclusive Race and Hispanic Origin – New York City Neighborhood Tabulation Areas*, 2010], Population Division – [[New York City]] Department of City Planning, March 29, 2011. Accessed June 14, 2016.</ref>

The entirety of Community Board 9, which covers Prospect Lefferts Gardens and Crown Heights South, had 98,650 inhabitants as of NYC Health's 2018 Community Health Profile, with an average life expectancy of 81.2 years.<ref name="CHP2018-9">{{Cite web|url=https://www1.nyc.gov/assets/doh/downloads/pdf/data/2018chp-bk9.pdf|title=South Crown Heights and Lefferts Gardens (Including Prospect Lefferts Gardens, South Crown Heights and Wingate)|date=2018|website=nyc.gov|publisher=NYC Health|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref>{{Rp|2, 20}} This is equal to the median life expectancy of all New York City neighborhoods.<ref name=":21">{{Cite web|url=https://www1.nyc.gov/assets/doh/downloads/pdf/tcny/community-health-assessment-plan.pdf|title=2016–2018 Community Health Assessment and Community Health Improvement Plan: Take Care New York 2020|date=2016|website=[[government of New York City|nyc.gov]]|publisher=[[New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene]]|access-date=September 8, 2017}}</ref>{{Rp|53 (PDF p. 84)}}<ref>{{cite web | title=New Yorkers are living longer, happier and healthier lives | website=New York Post | date=June 4, 2017 | url=https://nypost.com/2017/06/04/new-yorkers-are-living-longer-happier-and-healthier-lives/ | access-date=March 1, 2019}}</ref> Most inhabitants are middle-aged adults and youth: 22% are between the ages of 0 and 17, 30% between 25 and 44, and 25% between 45 and 64. The ratio of college-aged and elderly residents was lower, at 9% and 14% respectively.<ref name="CHP2018-9" />{{Rp|2}}

{{As of|2016}}, the median household income in Community Board 9 was $51,072.<ref name="CB9PUMA">{{cite web|url=https://censusreporter.org/profiles/79500US3604011-nyc-brooklyn-community-district-9-crown-heights-south-prospect-lefferts-wingate-puma-ny/|title=NYC-Brooklyn Community District 9—Crown Heights South, Prospect Lefferts & Wingate PUMA, NY|access-date=July 17, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306111336/https://censusreporter.org/profiles/79500US3604011-nyc-brooklyn-community-district-9-crown-heights-south-prospect-lefferts-wingate-puma-ny/ |archive-date=March 6, 2019 |url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2018, an estimated 22% of Crown Heights South residents lived in poverty, compared to 21% in all of Brooklyn and 20% in all of New York City. One in nine residents (11%) were unemployed, compared to 9% in the rest of both Brooklyn and New York City. Rent burden, or the percentage of residents who have difficulty paying their rent, is 55% in Crown Heights South, higher than the citywide and boroughwide rates of 52% and 51% respectively. Based on this calculation, {{as of|2018|lc=y}}, Crown Heights South is considered to be gentrifying.<ref name="CHP2018-9" />{{Rp|7}}

According to the 2020 census data from [[New York City Department of City Planning]], there were 20,000 to 29,999 Black residents, 10,000 to 19,999 White residents, and 5,000 to 9,999 Hispanic residents.<ref>{{cite web | title=Map: Race and ethnicity across the US | website=CNN | date=August 14, 2021 | url=https://www.cnn.com/interactive/2021/us/census-race-ethnicity-map/ | access-date=November 7, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www1.nyc.gov/assets/planning/download/pdf/planning-level/nyc-population/census2020/dcp_2020-census-briefing-booklet-1.pdf|title=Key Population & Housing Characteristics; 2020 Census Results for New York City|publisher=[[New York City Department of City Planning]]|date=August 2021|access-date=November 7, 2021|pages=21, 25, 29, 33}}</ref>

==Police and crime==

[[File:71 Pct NYPD Malbone St NY Av jeh.jpg|thumb|right|267px|71st Precinct]]

Prospect Lefferts Gardens is patrolled by the 71st Precinct of the [[New York City Police Department|NYPD]], located at 421 Empire Boulevard.<ref name="NYPD 71st Precinct">{{Cite web|url=https://www1.nyc.gov/site/nypd/bureaus/patrol/precincts/71st-precinct.page|title=NYPD – 71st Precinct|website=www.nyc.gov|publisher=[[New York City Police Department]]|access-date=October 3, 2016}}</ref> The 71st Precinct ranked 46th safest out of 69 patrol areas for per-capita crime in 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dnainfo.com/new-york/crime-safety-report/brooklyn/prospect-lefferts/|title=Prospect Lefferts Gardens & Crown Heights – DNAinfo.com Crime and Safety Report|website=www.dnainfo.com|access-date=October 6, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170415063740/https://www.dnainfo.com/new-york/crime-safety-report/brooklyn/prospect-lefferts|archive-date=April 15, 2017|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref> {{As of|2018}}, with a non-fatal assault rate of 73 per 1,000 people in Prospect Lefferts Gardens, rates of [[violent crime]]s per capita are greater than that of the city as a whole. The incarceration rate of 598 per 100,000 people is also greater than that of the city as a whole.<ref name="CHP2018-9" />{{Rp|8}}<ref name="CHP2018-9" />{{Rp|8}}

The 71st Precinct has a lower crime rate than in the 1990s, with crimes across all categories having decreased by 31% between 2010 and June 2025. The precinct reported 1 murder, 8 rapes, 51 robberies, 167 felony assaults, 32 burglaries, 142 grand larcenies, and 40 grand larcenies auto in the first half of 2025.<ref>{{Cite web| title=CompStat - Report Covering the Week | date=2018-04-08 | url=https://www.nyc.gov/assets/nypd/downloads/pdf/crime_statistics/cs-en-us-071pct.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413193345/http://www1.nyc.gov:80/assets/nypd/downloads/pdf/crime_statistics/cs-en-us-071pct.pdf | archive-date=2018-04-13}}</ref>

== Fire safety ==
The [[New York City Fire Department]] (FDNY) operates two fire stations in Prospect Lefferts Gardens.<ref>{{Cite FDNY locations}}</ref> Engine Co. 281/Ladder Co. 147 is located at 1210 Cortelyou Road,<ref>{{cite web | website=FDNYtrucks.com | title=Engine Company 281/Ladder Company 147 | url=http://www.fdnytrucks.com/files/html/brooklyn/e281.htm | access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> while Engine Co. 249/Ladder Co. 113 is located at 491 Rogers Avenue.<ref>{{cite web | website=FDNYtrucks.com | title=Engine Company 249/Ladder Company 113 | url=http://www.fdnytrucks.com/files/html/brooklyn/e249.htm | access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref>

== Health ==
{{As of|2018}}, [[preterm birth]]s in Prospect Lefferts Gardens and Crown Heights South are more common than in other places citywide, though births to teenage mothers are less common than in other places citywide. There were 91 preterm births per 1,000 live births in Prospect Lefferts Gardens (compared to 87 per 1,000 citywide) and 14.8 births to teenage mothers per 1,000 live births (compared to 19.3 per 1,000 citywide).<ref name="CHP2018-9" />{{Rp|11}} Both neighborhoods have a relatively high population of residents who are [[Health insurance coverage in the United States|uninsured]], or who receive healthcare through [[Medicaid]].<ref name=":14">[http://www.health.ny.gov/health_care/medicaid/redesign/dsrip/pps_applications/docs/maimonides_medical_center/3.8_maimonides_cna.pdf New York City Health Provider Partnership Brooklyn Community Needs Assessment: Final Report], [[New York Academy of Medicine]] (October 3, 2014).</ref> In 2018, this population of uninsured residents was estimated to be 16% in Prospect Lefferts Gardens, compared to the citywide rate of 12%.<ref name="CHP2018-9" />{{Rp|14}}

[[Air pollution]] is {{convert|0.0078|mg/m3|oz/ft3|sp=us}} in Prospect Lefferts Gardens, slightly higher than the citywide and boroughwide averages.<ref name="CHP2018-9" />{{Rp|9}} Eight percent of residents are [[Smoking|smokers]], compared to the city average of 14% of residents being smokers.<ref name="CHP2018-9" />{{Rp|13}} In Prospect Lefferts Gardens Crown Heights South, 32% of residents are obese, 15% are diabetic, and 37% have high blood pressure.<ref name="CHP2018-9" />{{Rp|16}} In addition, 19% of children are obese, compared to the citywide average of 20%.<ref name="CHP2018-9" />{{Rp|12}}

Eighty-one percent of Prospect Lefferts Gardens and Crown Heights South residents eat some fruits and vegetables every day, which is slightly lower than the city's average of 87%. In 2018, 84% of residents described their health as "good", "very good", or "excellent", compared to the city's average of 78%.<ref name="CHP2018-9" />{{Rp|13}} For every supermarket, there are 21 [[convenience store|bodegas]] in Prospect Lefferts Gardens and Crown Heights South.<ref name="CHP2018-9" />{{Rp|10}}

== Education ==
Prospect Lefferts Gardens generally has a similar ratio of college-educated residents to the rest of the city {{as of|2018|lc=y}}. While 35% of residents age 25 and older have a college education or higher, 16% have less than a high school education and 48% are high school graduates or have some college education. By contrast, 40% of Brooklynites and 38% of city residents have a college education or higher.<ref name="CHP2018-9" />{{Rp|6}} In Prospect Lefferts Gardens, reading achievement rose from 31 percent in 2000 to 37 percent in 2011, and math achievement rose from 21 percent to 47 percent within the same time period.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://furmancenter.org/files/sotc/BK_09_11.pdf|title=S. Crown Heights / Lefferts Gardens – BK 09|date=2011|publisher=[[Furman Center for Real Estate and Urban Policy]]|access-date=October 5, 2016}}</ref>

Prospect Lefferts Gardens' rates of elementary school student absenteeism are higher than the rest of New York City. The proportions of elementary school students who missed twenty or more days per [[school year]] were 22% in the neighborhood, compared to the citywide average of 20% of students.<ref name=":21" />{{Rp|24 (PDF p. 55)}}<ref name="CHP2018-9" />{{Rp|6}} Additionally, 77% of high school students graduate on time, compared to the citywide average of 75% of students.<ref name="CHP2018-9" />{{Rp|6}}

===Schools===

There are four public schools within the area's borders which are part of NYC School District 17. There are two middle schools: [http://schools.nyc.gov/SchoolPortals/17/K002/default.htm M.S. 002] for sixth to eighth graders and [http://www.ms61.org/ M.S. 61] which serves the sixth through ninth grades. [http://schools.nyc.gov/SchoolPortals/17/K092/default.htm P.S. 92] is an elementary school for kindergarten through fifth grade. In 2010, the [http://leffertsgardens.org/ Lefferts Gardens Charter School] opened an elementary program that focuses on environmental science and experiential learning.

===Library===
The [[Brooklyn Public Library]] (BPL)'s Crown Heights branch, on the border with Crown Heights, is located at 560 New York Avenue near Maple Street.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bklynlibrary.org/locations/crown-heights|title=Crown Heights Library|date=August 19, 2011|website=Brooklyn Public Library|access-date=February 21, 2019}}</ref>

== Transportation ==

[[File:Subway entrance sterling snow 20131214.jpg|thumb|right|250px|[[Sterling Street (IRT Nostrand Avenue Line)|Sterling Street]] subway station in northern Prospect-Lefferts Gardens.]]

Prospect Lefferts Gardens is serviced by the [[New York City Subway]]'s {{NYCS trains|Prospect Park}} at the [[Prospect Park (BMT Brighton Line)|Prospect Park]] station and the {{NYCS trains|Brighton local}} at the [[Parkside Avenue (BMT Brighton Line)|Parkside Avenue]] station (both on the [[BMT Brighton Line]]), as well as the [[Sterling Street (IRT Nostrand Avenue Line)|Sterling Street]] and [[Winthrop Street (IRT Nostrand Avenue Line)|Winthrop Street]] stations on the [[IRT Nostrand Avenue Line]] ({{NYCS trains|Nostrand}}). Additionally, the {{NYC bus link|B12|B16|B41|B43|B44|B44 SBS|B48|B49|prose=yes}} [[New York City Bus]] routes serve the area.<ref>{{Cite NYC bus map|B}}</ref>
